name: Zona 1 and Parque Centro America
tagline: The neoclassical centre, where the Spanish schools are
description: Xela's historic core around the colonnaded Parque Centro America, built in the neoclassical style during the coffee boom, holding the cathedral, the theatre, the municipal buildings and most of the city's Spanish schools, cafes and bars. Everything a visitor needs is inside a few blocks.
bestFor: Anyone here for the Spanish schools, with the cafes and bars on the doorstep
pros: Most Spanish schools and the international community here
cons: The highest rents in Xela, though still very low
Traffic and diesel fumes in the narrow streets

name: Zona 3 and La Democracia
tagline: The market district, where the city shops
description: The area around the Democracia market, Xela's main produce and goods market, spilling into the surrounding streets with a working, entirely Guatemalan character. It is cheaper than Zona 1, busier in the daytime, and the best place to see how the highland economy actually functions.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the market and local prices rather than the school quarter
pros: The main market and the lowest food prices
Genuinely local, with no tourist pricing
Ten minutes on foot to the central park
cons: Congested and noisy through the day
Few cafes or services for visitors

name: Zona 9 and La Pradera
tagline: The newer residential side, with the malls and quieter streets
description: The southeastern districts where Xela's middle class has built, with newer houses, supermarkets, the shopping centre and quieter residential streets. It is the most comfortable part of the city to live in and the least interesting, with a bus or taxi needed into the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern house and supermarkets rather than the old centre
pros: Supermarkets and the shopping centre nearby
Quieter and safer-feeling than the centre
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes into Zona 1
No character and little street life

name: Zunil and the Southern Valley
tagline: The Maya village down the valley, with the hot springs above it
description: A K'iche' village about ten kilometres south, built around a white church in a steep valley of terraced vegetable fields, with the Fuentes Georginas hot springs on the slope above and the Santa Maria volcano close. Traditional dress is everyday wear here rather than a display.
bestFor: Stays that want a traditional highland village and the hot springs
pros: Fuentes Georginas hot springs above the village
Living K'iche' culture and a genuine village market
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes into Xela
Almost no services and very little Spanish tuition
Cold at night with no heating

name: Llanos del Pinal
tagline: The plain below Santa Maria, where the volcano climb starts
description: A flat agricultural area southwest of the city at the foot of Santa Maria, from which the standard route up the volcano begins, with the active Santiaguito vent visible below the summit. Scattered houses, fields and views of the cone from every direction.
bestFor: Stays built around climbing Santa Maria and watching Santiaguito
pros: The Santa Maria trailhead a short walk away
Views of the volcano and the active vent
cons: Twenty minutes into Xela and transport is infrequent
Ashfall from Santiaguito when the wind turns
